comments.author: timmg
comments.story: What happened to Apple's legendary attention to detail?
comments.why: Ad mocking Windows security pop-ups, now ironic for Mac.
comments.text: I wonder if anyone else here is old enough to remember the "I'm a Mac", "And I'm a PC" ads. There was one that was about all the annoying security pop-ups Windows (used to?) have. (FWIW, it starts here: [VIDEO] .) Lately I've gotten so many of these popups on Mac that it both annoys and amuses the hell out of me. "Die a hero or live long enough to see yourself become the villain", I guess. But, man, Apple hardware still rocks. Can't deny that.

comments.author: ghshephard
comments.why: Apple's Mac vs PC ads as an example of its marketing.
comments.text: Fair enough - I agree that Microsoft has been shifting it's messaging quite a bit - but I think a lot of that has to do with Apple being a functional organization (singular vision directed on downwards) and Microsoft is a Divisional Organization (multiple business lines). Where the single vision is communicated (Windows Everywhere) - it's not always appropriate -(Consumers care about experience, not product lines) Here is the last few years of Apple Ads. o [VIDEO] (PC Ad) o [LINK] (iPod Ad) o [LINK] (Genius Ad) They have been hitting their stride recently: o [LINK] (iPhone Camera) o [LINK] (iPhone Facetime) o [LINK] (iPhone Music) Interesting, one of the supposedly "Worst reviewed" ads really spoke to me o [LINK] (Designed in California) I hope we see more like the last one. That's the sort of thing that I think a company should aspire to.
